intro: Look down. Before you opens Ihlara Valley, a rock settlement in Aksaray province, from the 9th–11th century AD. It is a canyon cut 100 metres deep by the Melendiz river, and its walls are honeycombed with frescoed rock churches.
history: Patiently, the Melendiz river cut a fourteen-kilometre gorge a hundred metres deep into the volcanic plateau. In the Byzantine period, more than a hundred churches and chapels were carved into its walls. Their frescoes fall into two styles: the local Cappadocian manner, with its eastern influence, and the court style of Constantinople. Two worlds, standing side by side in one valley.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Kokar Church and the Snake Church, then the Ağaçaltı Church and the Sümbüllü Church — and finish in the village of Belisırma.
facts: Did you know? More than three hundred steps lead down into the gorge, and its floor stays markedly cooler than the plateau in summer — one reason monastic life favoured it. The valley runs fourteen kilometres and reaches a hundred metres deep, with more than a hundred churches and chapels cut into its walls. And the frescoes hold two worlds together: the local Cappadocian manner shows eastern influence, while other churches in the same valley are painted in the court style of Constantinople.
outro: This brings our journey through Ihlara Valley to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These painted walls have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your walk.
